transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2028-03-19
- Time: 16:00 UTC / 11:00 ET
- Duration: ~58 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Jules (Redwood CSM), Ravi (Lucent CTO), Claire (Head of ML), Ben (Infra Lead), Sofia (DevOps), Adele (Product)

Summary:
Quick kickoff-style sync to align on onboarding cadence, infra access, security needs (SOC2/SAML/KMS), and to agree next steps for a pilot on Redwood Dedicated. Customer wants predictable latency for inference in a regulated medical image-annotation workflow; cost sensitivity is moderate and latency SLO is primary.

Topics covered:
- Runbook & access checklist
- VPC / peering / on-prem connectivity options
- Data residency and audit log expectations
- Dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs (cost vs latency)
- Pilot scope: 2 models (embedding + chat completion) with 50 concurrent users
- Measurements: p95 latency target, token throughput, KV cache hit expectations

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for taking the time, uh we'll keep this pretty practical — today's to line up runbook, access, and next steps for the pilot. quick intros?
[00:12] Ravi (Lucent): Ravi here, CTO. Appreciate it. We're trying to get Redwood into our inference lane for a pilot with our annotator tooling — latency's the big one.
[00:22] Claire (Lucent): Claire, head of ML. We'll be driving the prompt sets and quality evals. we have some privacy constraints so we need to validate data residency options.
[00:30] Ben (Lucent): Ben, infra. I'll own peering / networking. we probably need an on-prem option or VPC peering depending on final SLA.
[00:38] Ethan (Redwood): Ethan, solutions eng — I'll drive the technical intake and run a quick perf baseline.
[00:43] Jules (Redwood): Jules, CSM, I'll coordinate onboarding milestones and the playbook.
[00:48] Adele (Lucent): Adele, product — aligning on success criteria and timelines.

[02:01] Maya: cool. high level — Lucent's success criteria? Adele or Ravi, do you want to lay that out quick?
[02:10] Adele: Sure. we want p95 under 800ms for short completions, batch embedding at throughput of ~200 requests/minute, and stable costs under a threshold we agreed internally. also SOC2 compliance and audit logs visibility.
[02:28] Ravi: yes, also ability to operate in a private VPC or on-prem sealed box if needed for certain PII workflows.

[03:10] Ethan: quick clarifying Q — when you say p95 < 800ms, is that cold-start inclusive? or warm-path only?
[03:18] Claire: mostly warm-path; cold-starts are acceptable at higher latency but we'd like caching and prefix reuse to minimize that.

[04:05] Ethan: okay makes sense. for warm-paths we can usually get those latencies with Dedicated capacity and tuned batching. hosted can be close too but Dedicated gives you predictability.

[05:10] Ben: what's the effort on our side to enable Dedicated? we have to coordinate VPC peering, IAM roles, and possibly KMS integration.
[05:21] Jules: we'll provide an access checklist — it's basically three things: network peering/cidr exchanges, service account keys or cross-account role, and a KMS key wrap if you want customer-managed keys.

[06:02] Ben: ok that sounds straight forward. any special firewall rules?
[06:09] Ethan: standard — allow outbound to Redwood egress IPs on 443, we'll share CIDR blocks. For on-prem we can run a Private agent but that needs a different setup; we'll document both paths. (slight hesitation) You'll probably need a NAT gateway for egress if traffic originates from an isolated subnet.

[07:45] Claire: about data retention — we cannot have persistent logs of raw patient text in Redwood-hosted storage for the clinical pilot. Can you confirm options?
[07:55] Maya: yes — we have options: hosted with log redaction and short retention, Dedicated with customer-controlled retention, or Private (VPC/on-prem) where logs never leave your environment. we'll surface the security docs.

[08:40] Adele: and can you provide SOC 2 docs and SAML SSO flow for our auditors?
[08:46] Jules: absolutely, we'll attach SOC2 Type II, ISO summary, and SAML setup guide. we'll include KMS/HSM integration notes.

[10:12] Ravi: timeline — we want pilot running inside 4 weeks. realistic?
[10:19] Maya: yes, with standard onboarding we've seen 3-6 weeks depending on how quickly infra access is provided. if Ben's team can fill the access form and we get keys the week of 3/20, pilot deploy by 4/15 is doable.

[11:00] Ben: I can start the form today. question on model variants — we plan to use a finetuned embedding model and a smaller chat LLM. do you recommend quantization or smaller variants to save cost?
[11:15] Ethan: for embeddings, quantization is low-risk and can cut memory/cost. for chat, it depends on quality tolerance — we can suggest a quantized variant for latency-sensitive paths and keep a higher-precision fallback. Redwood Optimize will surface recommendations based on your token mix.

[13:30] Claire: can we run a short benchmark? like 1000 samples with canonical prompts to measure p95 and token cost?
[13:38] Ethan: yes, we'll run a baseline on Hosted and Dedicated variants. we'll need your prompt set and concurrency profile.

[14:12] Maya: action item there — Claire to provide sample prompts & expected concurrency. Ethan to run baseline and share spreadsheet with p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens.

[15:40] Ben: networking follow-up: do you support private peering or only public egress?
[15:46] Ethan: both. VPC peering is supported in most regions; where peering isn't possible we provide a managed NAT egress or private link equivalent. we'll correlate options to latency tradeoffs.

[17:20] Sofia (Lucent): small ops note — we have strict change windows. peering work might have to happen on weekends.
[17:27] Jules: we'll make onboarding flexible, and coordinate with your windows.

[18:50] Claire: compliance question — audit logs need to surface token-level metadata but not raw payloads. is that supported?
[18:58] Maya: yes, we can configure audit logs to include telemetry (latency, model, route, token counts) while redacting payloads. and you can forward logs to your SIEM (we support Splunk/Datadog) or ship them to your S3.

[20:05] Adele: are there any special contractual SLAs for Dedicated? also runbook for rollouts & canary?
[20:13] Maya: Dedicated has SLA options; we'll include the SLA matrix in the follow-up. rollouts / canaries are supported in the console; we'll share a quickstart on creating canary traffic and automatic fallback policies.

[21:30] Ravi: pricing — can you give a ballpark for a reserved capacity that meets our needs: 50 concurrent, mixed embeddings + chat, and say 2M tokens/day?
[21:41] Maya: rough ballpark now: reserved monthly for Dedicated with that profile — we'll model different quantization scenarios. Ethan will prepare a sizing worksheet and a cost range.

[23:10] Claire: one more technical — how do you manage KV cache across multiple workers? our pipelines expect caches to be shared for low-latency multi-turn flows.
[23:22] Ethan: Redwood runtime manages KV cache sharding with sticky routing on session tokens; for Dedicated we can configure co-located workers to improve local cache hits. occasionally transcripts call it K V cash in older docs, so excuse the audio transcripts.

[25:00] Ben: if we do Private on-prem, what's the support model? thicker ops on our side?
[25:09] Jules: Private adds a managed control plane in your environment; we provide deployment runbooks, and a support SLA can include on-call from Redwood infra for rollout periods.

[27:40] Adele: success metrics recap — p95 < 800ms, embedding throughput 200/min, cost threshold TBD, pilot duration 6 weeks.
[27:52] Maya: yep. we'll call that the pilot SLO and track with the console. we'll also wire up evals to detect regressions against Claire's prompt set.

[30:05] Claire: for evals, we use human-annotated quality checks. does Redwood support hooking those into alerts?
[30:14] Ethan: yes — Redwood Optimize can compare baseline vs current model outputs on a prompt set and trigger regression alerts. we'll show a sample chart.

[32:00] Maya: ok let's nail down next steps and owners.
[32:10] Maya: first, Maya/Jules will share the onboarding runbook and access checklist by Tue 3/21.
[32:18] Jules: include SOC2 and SAML docs in that packet.
[32:22] Ben: Ben will complete infra access form by Wed 3/22 and block change window for peering.
[32:30] Claire: Claire will share 3 canonical prompt sets and expected concurrency shape by Thu 3/23.
[32:36] Ethan: I'll run the baseline on Hosted + Dedicated variants and send the sizing worksheet by Sat 3/24.
[32:43] Maya: we'll also include a pricing ballpark in that worksheet.

[35:00] Ravi: one operational ask — can you provide a short training for our annotators on how to interpret model outputs and fallback behavior?
[35:10] Jules: yes, we can run a 30–45 minute enablement session during pilot week 1.

[36:12] Adele: any constraints re: data residency in EU zones? we have a research team in EU.
[36:20] Maya: yes, we can pin region deployments and ensure logs/data residency in EU. we'll note region options in the runbook.

[38:05] Ben: question on keys — do you accept HSM-wrapped keys from AWS KMS or do you require Redwood-managed keys?
[38:13] Ethan: we support customer-managed keys via KMS; we also have an integration guide for external HSMs — we'll include the steps.

[40:40] Claire: curious about A/B rollouts: can we route a small %, like 5%, to a cheaper quantized model and monitor quality?
[40:48] Ethan: yes, rollouts and traffic splitting are first-class; console supports percentage-based routing and automatic fallback to the primary model on error or quality drop.

[42:30] Maya: anything else before we wrap?
[42:36] Adele: no, this is good. please also include a short runbook for incident response and contact list.
[42:45] Jules: will do.

[44:00] Maya: recap of deliverables: runbook + security docs (Maya/Jules), infra form (Ben), prompts (Claire), baseline + sizing (Ethan), enablement session scheduling (Jules).
[44:12] Maya: aim to reconvene after baseline — propose Fri 3/31 for follow-up; does that work?
[44:21] Ravi: works for me.
[44:24] Ben: works.

[46:00] Sofia: small note — our perf windows are Pacific weekend nights, we'll share exact slots in the infra form.
[46:06] Jules: noted.

[50:00] Maya: ok thanks everyone — we'll send the packet and confirm calendar invites.
[50:06] Claire: thanks — excited to get moving.
[50:09] Ravi: thanks all.

End transcript.
